newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle feeders await cold - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle feeders await cold - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains cattle feeders were bracing themselves for extremely cold weather set to push temperatures below zero in the Panhandle area by midweek.
The cold weather could stress cattle and slow weight gains resulting in the possibility of $66.00 to $67.00 per cwt being paid for cattle this week, steady to $1.00 higher than last week's trade.
Owners were pricing cattle at $68.00 and expecting packers to bid $65.00 once bids surface, one Panhandle source said.
The Panhandle-areas showlist was projected to be about the same size as last week's 60,000-head, sources said.
Supplies of market-ready cattle on the showlists remained tight, which could lend further support to prices this week, several feedlot sources said.

Cattle price gains could be limited if there is no wet weather along with this week's forecast cold in the Panhandle and Plains, said Dale Benson, livestock analyst with Dean Witter Reynolds in Chicago. Benson said wet and cold weather would stress livestock more than just cold.
